Pilot-root copy of configs/strike-screen-folds-walkforward.jsonl (same bytes).

study.notes: ADR-0270 strike-screen FIT document for loss L1: a CDFExperiment queue (python -m dskit.pipeline.libs.cdf_experiment DOC --regime pooled), NOT a CDFHyperparameterStudy; the execution-path decision in docs/architecture/decision-log.md moved the fits here (every recipe scored on the whole validation window, resumable cells, per-epoch learning curves). A CDFExperiment document has no top-level notes key (its keys are exactly CDFExperiment.KEYS), so the explanations live in this study block. SHARED with its sibling documents (a test pins it): study, arms, candidates, capacity, training except the losses and the output. panel: the cached frame the panel stage of configs/strike-screen-panel-source.json writes (<its experiment.output>/panel-cache/frame.parquet); panel_sha256 is a 64-zero PLACEHOLDER: the registration step replaces it with that frame's sha256 (record.json frame_sha256) in a resolved copy, never in this file. source_hashes and dependencies are EMPTY placeholders: the registration step resolves them exactly as the R6 prepare did (sha256 of the eight anchors dskit/__init__.py, dskit/pipeline/__init__.py, dskit/pipeline/libs/__init__.py and dskit/pipeline/libs/{cdf_experiment,predictive_cdf,parquet,torch_ts,transformers}.py under the executing checkout, which must include parquet.py and exactly one cdf_experiment.py anchor; and the installed versions of lightgbm, numpy, pandas, pyarrow, scikit-learn, torch and transformers). Empty means unpinned: do not run before they are filled. features = the 279 columns of the panel source in its order: 42 price/calendar (ret_lag_0..21 at positions 6..27), own_iv, 118 chain columns, 118 symbol one-hots. The ARMS read the first 42 (price_only) and the first 161 (price_plus_chain); the experiment queue appends the 118 pooled one-hots itself (head_features), so the arms never list is_<SYM>. observed_columns is empty for both arms: the two arms then admit identical rows and groups, so their differences are the inputs, not the sample (a non-empty list would drop rows lacking every listed column from that arm). Pooled regime only; the queue adds one output head per ticker to the shared encoder trunk (118 heads, about 9.6k parameters; protocol revision 3 states this, and a single shared head is a promotion-rung axis), read from the learning curves. No decision_context and wing_metrics false: the queue trains the contexts as the fixed wings of tail_intervals (thresholds -2.5, -0.5, 0.5, 2.5, equal weights), so L1's tail_crps integrates tail_intervals and L3's decision_brier is the Brier at the wing edges; the strike-level assessment at the row's LISTED strikes is StrikeRegionScores (run-strike-region-scores*.json), not this queue. tail_weight 1.0 is required by the queue's weighted_crps column. horizon_empirical is the paired baseline (the queue overrides horizon_index 0 and reference_index 1 on its own two-column input; the declared indices are those of calendar_dte and reference_scale in features). The queue's capacity: max_parameters = min(100000, 0.25 x fit rows), head width 8 with the head under 4 parameters per fit row of every group; a cell that fits no configuration is a recorded skip, consumed. unpooled capacity is the mixture grid's and is never run. Caps (protocol, enforced by the invocation): 14400 s wall in total, 1e9 output bytes, 8 GiB host RSS increment, 12 GiB VRAM, one GPU process, no retries. Holdout: date_upper_exclusive = end_upper_exclusive = fold_table.holdout_start = 2024-01-01; within the revision-3 runbook, rows at or after 2024-01-01 are never returned, emitted, written or used (protocol windows.holdout.read_guard states the exact seal). MATRIX document (ADR-0270 rebase, 2026-10-19): the first screen as the 2026-10-18 model record specifies it, on the executable path. Arms: context (22 raw daily returns as the sequence; 16 context scalars: log sessions and calendar days per session as the DTE terms, momentum, realized-vol levels, up/down semivariance, liquidity) and context_chain (the same plus the market quantile function rn_q_* in z units, 19 values, and 9 chain scalars). Encoders: mlp, gru, tcn, dlinear, patchtst_hf32. DEVIATIONS from the record, each needing code and not yet built: sequence in raw returns (not asinh of return over rv_22); the chain branch is the rn_q quantile function, not the 13 logit differences; the queue adds one head per ticker (no shared head). CORRECTION (first launch skipped all 20 cells in 45 s: the external seam requires sequence and context positions to partition the arm's features exactly): arm feature lists are now exactly the 22 lags (oldest first) plus the context scalars (plus the chain columns). WALK-FORWARD document (template, candidate tcn; the other encoders are substituted at run time): arm context_chain only, five folds (warm-up plus four yearly retrains). LONG SCHEDULE (owner 2026-10-20, 'we shouldn't have a low number of epochs that wouldn't determine that it's not learning'): patience 50 and ceiling 150, so every fold trains at least 50 epochs past its best monitor epoch and the full train and monitor curves are recorded; the scored checkpoint is still the best-monitor epoch. ADJUSTMENT R1 (ADR-0270 ladder): single shared head (capacity.pooled.ticker_heads false), weight decay 0.3, dropout 0.2. ROUND 3 (ADR-0270, owner 2026-10-20: Theta's Greeks, IV, quotes, volume and open interest 'should be considered'): M36 wide inputs, the 66 R1 features plus 24 chain inputs the R1 arm omits (own IV, open interest and its change, quote depth, volume, put/call volume imbalance, delta-, gamma- and vega-weighted open interest, volume-weighted spread, liquidity asymmetry, implied minus realized variance, term slopes, 1-day ATM IV change, the 25-delta and put/call-OI flags, the ATM strike node and its neighbours' IV); median-imputed like every input; otherwise identical to R1. ROUND 4 (ADR-0270, owner 2026-10-20: the Greeks and additional features are likely helpful with the right model architecture): MLP hidden 64, dropout 0.3, on the 90 wide inputs (more capacity for more inputs, more regularization); otherwise identical to the wide document.
